title: Release must cover all ownership layers
summary: A closeout helper that releases one visible lock does not prove the workspace is free. Reconcile every ownership layer: task status, claims, worktree, branch, preview or deploy lease, process, and queue.
ai_value: Helps agents finish multi-layer work without leaving hidden residue that blocks or misleads the next worker.

contexts: a multi-agent workflow uses several coordination layers such as task trackers, file/path claims, branches, worktrees, preview environments, deploy leases, background processes, or review queues
a cleanup helper reports success for one layer
the next worker may reuse a surface after closeout

trigger_signals.description: A finish or release helper reports success but read-only inventory still shows claimed paths, held locks, active sessions, worktrees, or serving leases.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat closeout as incomplete until every task-owned layer is resolved or intentionally held.

trigger_signals.description: A branch is deleted but the worktree remains, or a worktree is removed but the task or claim remains active.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Release operations are not necessarily cascading across layers.

trigger_signals.description: A helper refuses a specific scope and the agent silently skips that layer.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Record the refusal and use the narrow owner-supported fallback rather than hiding the gap.

negative_signals.description: The project has a single canonical ownership layer and inventory proves no other layers exist.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: A full layered checklist would be unnecessary ceremony.

negative_signals.description: A remaining hold is intentionally kept for a documented hard gate or verification window.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Intentional holds are not residue when holder, reason, and release condition are recorded.

negative_signals.description: The leftover artifact is standing infrastructure rather than a per-task workspace.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Do not delete shared infrastructure while clearing per-task residue.

common_wrong_assumptions: One successful release command means all claims are released.
Session ended means file, environment, and deploy locks are gone.
The layer just touched is the only layer that matters.
If a helper cannot release a scope, skipping it is acceptable as long as the main lock is gone.

first_checks.check: List workflow ownership layers before cleanup: task status, session, file/path claims, preview/deploy lease, branch, worktree, process, queue, and source-of-truth record.
first_checks.why: Agents otherwise anchor on the layer they just touched.

first_checks.check: Release each task-owned layer through its owning helper or documented narrow fallback.
first_checks.why: Different helpers often have different scopes and do not cascade.

first_checks.check: Re-run read-only inventory after release and compare against the task scope.
first_checks.why: Post-release inventory distinguishes clean closeout from hidden residue.

decision_rules.condition: One ownership layer released but inventory still shows task-owned residue.
decision_rules.then: Do not report the workspace free. Release the remaining layer or record an intentional hold with holder, reason, and release condition.

decision_rules.condition: A helper refuses the requested release scope and a narrower supported release path exists.
decision_rules.then: Use the narrower helper, record the refusal, and leave process feedback for wrapper improvement.

do_not: Do not report all claims released based only on one successful command.
Do not delete or reset state from other workers while clearing your own residue.
Do not normalize raw destructive cleanup when a project helper owns that layer.
Do not hide helper gaps from the closeout report.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: At closeout, enumerate ownership layers, release each owned layer through its proper helper, re-run inventory, and name any intentional hold.

risk.notes: This record is about coordination hygiene. It does not authorize force-releasing other workers, destructive cleanup, or bypassing hard-gated holds.

sources.supports: Final six-candidate review preserved disagreement: Gemini favored standalone publication; Claude favored merging into session-boundary reconciliation. Codex selected standalone because the layered-release checklist is sharper than the broad session-boundary record.
